welcome.label: Welcome · the last pit
welcome.script:
Welcome back, engineers! Remember the quarry vote in Palmetto Springs?

[ON SCREEN: Old rock pits]
When a quarry finishes digging, it leaves a pit like these, full of water. So what should a pit become?

[ON SCREEN: Three designs]
June has three designs on her drafting table: a bird lake, a water reservoir, or a floating solar farm. Which is best? And could the best one get even better? Press Listen on June’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · limit or goal? (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🚧 Limit or goal?
parts.title: Two kinds of rules
rows: GOAL: score it, more is better

warmup.script:
(Hold up a ruler.) Say I need a pencil that fits in my pencil box. That’s a limit. It fits, or it doesn’t.

(Hold up two pencils.) But I also want one that writes smoothly. That’s a goal. One pencil can be better than another.

[ON SCREEN: Limit or goal?]
In the game, sort the town’s plan for the last pit. Is each card a limit or a goal? Then tell us which city water idea you like. Press Listen.

part2.label: Part 2 · build the matrix (Clues 2 and 3)

parts.label: 📊 Build the matrix
parts.title: Score every box
rows: Tap a ? box and read the evidence.

parts.label: 🔧 Make it better
parts.title: Borrow a feature
parts.body: Every goal at least ⭐⭐, and stay inside the budget.

part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: Build the matrix]
A decision matrix is a chart that scores every design on every goal. Tap each box, read the evidence, and give it stars. Then check the budget. Watch what happens to the solar farm!

[ON SCREEN: Make it better]
Two designs will tie. So be an engineer: pick one, and borrow a feature from another design to make it better, without going over the budget. Press Listen.

explore.label: Part 4 · test it small (Clue 4)
explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: A real reservoir]
This is real! Florida’s L-8 Reservoir used to be a rock mine. Now it stores water for the Everglades.

[ON SCREEN: Test it small]
Before building the real thing, engineers test a small model. Run each test on June’s model and watch the water. If something goes wrong, pick the revision that fixes it, then test again. That’s your last clue. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What should the last pit become?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Crack the case at the top of this tab: what should the last pit become, and how can the town make it better?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report. Two short answers, your own decision matrix in Part C, and a CER. Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Your answers save as you type. Press Listen.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “If we just pick the smartest scientist’s first idea, we’ll always get the best solution.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says we should just pick the smartest scientist’s first idea. Hmm. Did the first designs win today? What happened when you tested the model?

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Remember CER. Tap your side and two facts from today. Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 📐 Your specimen
parts.title: Blueprint of the last pit
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Forces of change
parts.body: How do natural events change Florida’s land, ecosystems and people?

closing.script:
Case closed, engineers! You compared, improved and tested, and you wrapped up the whole quarter.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and the blueprint of the last pit goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next week, a new kind of problem: what happens to Florida’s land, animals and people when a big storm hits? Press Listen for June’s last word.

part3.label: Part 3 · four Florida challenges
part3.script: Florida engineers face lots of challenges like ours. Tap each one to see the solutions and the revision an engineer might try. Notice how often the best idea combines two solutions. Press Listen.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
